What does inquiry at WIS mean?

In a world where answers are readily available, where information is accessible in abundance, it's more important than ever for students to develop skills in analysis and critical thinking. WIS students are encouraged to ask questions, to challenge assertions, and to think deeply about what they are learning.

The inquiry-based approach is emphasized in the IB Primary Years Program (Preschool to Grade 5) and the IB Diploma Program (Grades 11–12) as well as in the Project Zero methodologies used in all WIS grades. Visitors to WIS classrooms regularly comment on WIS students' perceptive questions.

pages.title: Guiding WIS Students to Ireland
blocks: Guiding WIS Students to Ireland: Sharing My Expertise with Counselors Across the U.S.
by Pam Joos, Co-Director of University Counseling

I was honored to be selected by Enterprise Ireland, through its Education in Ireland initiative, to present at their Counselor Webinar Guide Your Students to Ireland on September 29. Speaking alongside fellow U.S. counselors, I shared why Ireland is such a popular university destination for American students, and what our experience at WIS has taught us about guiding students through the process.
Our students apply to universities around the world, so I was glad to bring a global perspective to the conversation. Here are some of the key ideas I shared.

1. Ireland offers world-class academics and real-world experience in a welcoming setting. Irish universities are internationally respected, with innovative courses and internship opportunities at global companies. For many students, this combination of academic rigor and a warm, supportive culture makes the transition abroad feel manageable and exciting.

2. Students can focus on their field from day one. Many Irish degree programs are built around a chosen field from the start, rather than a broad general-education requirement. For students who already know their direction, this can be a real advantage. Medicine and law are offered as undergraduate degrees, with distinct routes for international applicants, so students can begin professional study right after high school. In the past few years, several WIS students have entered Irish universities to study medicine directly from high school.

3. Flexibility exists too. For students who aren't ready to commit to one field, some Irish universities offer broad entry routes that let them sample several subjects before choosing a specialization.
4. IB DP students are well prepared. The rigor, independence, and global outlook that come with the IB Diploma Program translate well to Irish university expectations.

I'm grateful to Enterprise Ireland for the invitation and to the counselors who joined and asked such thoughtful questions. WIS families, I look forward to talking through the possibilities in Ireland whenever your student is ready to begin exploring.
